_comment: Real trending/commercial songs for short-form use, per the channel owner's explicit 2026-07-27 decision to lift the CC0-only audio requirement for short-form (see config/gates.json short_form_gates.audio_license_gate for the full rationale/risk acceptance). These are NOT copyright-free — Content ID will likely mute/claim revenue on these, and repeated strikes risk channel termination. This file exists so every track used has documented provenance (source video, real identification) rather than an unverified guess. Agent 3.1 pulls from here or state/cc0_audio_library.json.

risk_acceptance.decided_by: channel owner, explicit choice after being presented three options (use real songs / stay CC0 / CC0-styled middle ground)
risk_acceptance.risk_disclosed: Content ID near-certain match on these (unlike the obscure/unidentifiable video clips), possible mute/claim, and repeated copyright strikes can lead to channel termination (YouTube's 3-strike policy).

owner_provided_sounds_drive_folder.purpose: Channel owner's shared Drive folder for dropping in audio files they find themselves, for Agent 3.1/4.2 to pull into this library. Check this folder each cycle (or when the owner mentions adding something) for new files: search Drive with `parentId = '1zmIRCIK9s_8886iRwhTBOabGDtS7CwIK'`. As of the note above, the folder only contained unrelated screen-recording .mp4 files ('Recording <timestamp>.mp4'), no audio yet — re-check for actual audio files before assuming there's nothing new. When a real audio file does show up, verify it the same way as any other track here (confirm it's a real playable audio file via ffprobe, get whatever title/artist info the owner provides or is embedded in the file's metadata, download it into assets/audio/trending/ or assets/audio/ as appropriate, and add a proper entry to this file or state/cc0_audio_library.json depending on its license).

unidentified_owner_provided_tracks._comment: 10 audio tracks extracted 2026-07-27 from screen-recording videos the owner uploaded to the Drive folder above (files named 'Recording <timestamp>.mp4'). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE from the tracks[] entries above: those were identified via yt-dlp's real track/artist metadata from a specific TikTok post. These have NO such metadata — they're raw screen recordings of some app playing car/lifestyle B-roll with background audio, and no on-screen UI in any of the 10 videos showed a song/sound name to identify against. Per direct instruction, only the audio was extracted/used — the video content itself was not used as source footage and was discarded (not added to assets/short-form-clips/raw/). Title/artist are genuinely unknown for all 10 — do not guess or invent one. Treat these as carrying at least as much Content-ID risk as the identified trending tracks above (arguably more, since there's no way to check ahead of time what they'll match against), under the same owner risk-acceptance in config/gates.json short_form_gates.audio_license_gate.
unidentified_owner_provided_tracks.usage_guidance: Tempo values are real (librosa beat detection), so these can still be picked by energy/pace for a candidate even without knowing the song. All are short native clips (8-25s) — scripts/short_form_transform.py loops/beat-tiles them the same as any other track, no special handling needed.

rotation_guidance: 8 identified tracks + 10 unidentified owner-provided tracks as of 2026-07-27. Check state/posted_history.json / recent state/short_form_queue.json entries before picking one — don't reuse the same track for consecutive shorts (same rule as state/cc0_audio_library.json). Match mood to angle: VEKI VEKI/Montagem/Ice Spice/Danza Kuduro/Gata Only variants for aggressive-energy angles (grind, hustle, proof-of-work); Love Nwantiti (Acoustic) or Tourner Dans Le Vide for warmer/more emotional or dramatic angles where pure aggression doesn't fit the theme; the unidentified owner-provided tracks can be picked by their measured tempo_bpm when nothing else fits. All native clips are short (7-25s) — scripts/short_form_transform.py loops and beat-tiles them automatically for any target duration, no manual handling needed.
